title: Pressure–lipid coupling gives no demonstrated incremental prediction of angiographic coronary disease across two institutions
abstract: We tested whether an interaction of resting systolic blood pressure and total cholesterol contains predictive information omitted by flexible additive conventional measurements. A fixed model was fitted to 303 Cleveland patients and evaluated without target refitting in 261 complete-case Hungarian patients from a separate institution. Adding the registered interaction changed Brier score from 0.157613 to 0.156957, a gain of 0.000656 (joint source–target stratified bootstrap 95% interval −0.009836 to 0.007835). AUC changed from 0.841430 to 0.842369. Source cross-validation slightly worsened. The prespecified evidence criterion was not met: this representation has no demonstrated incremental predictive benefit, rather than evidence of equivalence or absence of physiological interaction.
